I'm a data scientist and ML researcher. I work on making LLM evaluation trustworthy: knowing which model is actually better, and when its output can be trusted, when the labels, judges, and budgets behind the answer are imperfect.

For eleven years I've shipped machine learning to production. The question underneath all of it has been the same: when can you trust the model, and when does a human need to check? It ran through drive-failure and anomaly detection at Western Digital, revenue forecasting and consultant-assignment optimization at AWS, and audit reduction in a title-automation pipeline at First American. Now I study it for LLMs, where even the ground truth is increasingly generated by AI. My research is on [the Research page](research.qmd).

I care about the software around the models as much as the models: releases, CI/CD, code review, and being on call when something breaks.
